title: Provenance enables process-level evaluation beyond output scoring
content:
## Claim

Output-level benchmarks reward correct answers from broken processes the same as sound ones (Gettier applied to agents). Provenance makes reliabilist evaluation operational.

## Process questions unlocked

- **Skill contribution** — which skills correlate with correct outcomes vs contextslop
- **Mechanism reliability** — inference vs retrieval-and-paraphrase vs guessing
- **Failure localization** — which operation/skill introduced the error
- **Counterfactual replay** — re-run the log with one skill removed

These are queries against a provenance graph, not new metric inventions.

## Methodology grounding
The claims below live in the plugin's `data/methodology/` corpus; the relationship is stated per claim.

- **[[agents are simultaneously methodology executors and subjects creating a unique trust asymmetry]]** — BUILDS_ON. Output scoring evaluates the executor role only. Process-level evaluation is what the subject role requires, and the methodology claim explains why the agent cannot supply it itself: it does not perceive the mechanisms constraining it.
- **[[agent session boundaries create natural automation checkpoints that human-operated systems lack]]** — RELATES_TO. Both argue that the interesting evaluation happens at boundaries rather than in the middle of the work, where the actor is least able to observe itself.
description: Output scoring cannot distinguish reliable inference from lucky correct answers; an operation log makes skill contribution and failure localization queryable.
